title: Q2 Initiative: Hosted API + Model Catalog — Quarterly Plan & OKR Mapping
creator: Elena Park
description: Objective: Produce a concrete Q2 execution plan that aligns Hosted API product enhancements with the Model Catalog curation roadmap and maps to measurable OKRs. Deliverables: 1) Initiative map tying each catalog and API milestone to 2–3 OKRs (adoption, latency, cost per token, accuracy), 2) Release cadence and gating criteria for the May launch, 3) Canary and rollback plan for model-swap flows, 4) Cross-team staffing and dependency tracker. Background: With increased enterprise demand for predictable latency and curated model variants, we need a tightly coordinated quarter plan that balances the model catalog's curation and compatibility work with Hosted API features (model aliasing, streaming improvements, and model downgrade fallbacks). This ticket consolidates the PM-level decisions, success metrics, and required engineering/design scopes for the quarter.
success_metrics: Increase hosted-api monthly active customers using curated models by 30%
Reduce median 95th percentile latency for generation routes by 15%
Decrease per-token cost for top-3 workloads by 12%
0 major quality regressions detected in canary tests prior to prod rollouts
milestones: 2026-03-15: Finalize OKR mappings and initiative owners
2026-03-29: Complete requirements doc and API contract sketch
2026-04-15: Engineering spike and initial perf targets
2026-05-15: Model catalog curation complete for initial set
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model quantization causes quality drift - Mitigation: maintain non-quantized canary path + prompt-based evals
Risk: Autoscaling capacity hits peak causing tail latency - Mitigation: set burst capacity and conservative autoscale thresholds for the first 2 weeks
Risk: Catalog tagging mismatch leads to model swap incompatibilities - Mitigation: enforce catalog schema validation and add pre-deploy compatibility tests
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): API + catalog integration testbeds in staging with synthetic load. Phase 2 (canary): 5% traffic to curated-model path in us-west with detailed telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates). Phase 3 (ramped): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks if SLOs are met. Rollback triggers: >=3% error increase sustained for 30m, 20% regression in key eval prompts, or 25% rise in p99 latency.
notes: Decision: prefer canary-with-fallback over dark-launch to observe real production behavior while protecting user experience
Trade-off discussed: faster rollout vs. broader canary coverage; recommended two-week ramp with conservative thresholds
Follow-ups: schedule weekly syncs with runtime and catalog owners, add dedicated telemetry dashboard card for OKR metrics
